title: fast-path fallback bridge and tenant SLO temporal quiesce (hotfix)
author: Sofia Ramirez
description:
Motivation: During the 2026-02-27 regional incident we observed long-lived tenant circuit closures caused by an interaction between tenant KV cache eviction and the slowpath serving broker. This PR introduces a fast-path fallback bridge that quickly reroutes requests for affected tenants to a lightweight stateless slowpath handler and a temporal quiesce window for SLO enforcement to avoid rapid oscillation between open/closed circuits.

What this changes: single continuous block describing design and implementation: 1) new controller fast_path_bridge that detects candidate tenants from the SLO enforcer and marks them as 'fast-fallback' for a short TTL; 2) a stateless HTTP slowpath handler (runtime/slowpath_fallback) that can serve minimal responses, preserve KV cache warmup hints, and respond with clear retry-backoff hints to clients; 3) SLO enforcer updates to emit a 'quiesce' window when a tenant's circuit transitions to degraded to prevent immediate reopen attempts (backoff jitter is applied); 4) telemetry additions: fast_fallback.count, fast_fallback.duration_ms, quiesce.window_seconds, and a new alert rule for persistent fast-fallbacks (>5m).

Backwards compatibility and safety: the bridge is opt-in via a runtime feature flag (FEATURE_FAST_FALLBACK) and defaulted off for Dedicated customers; the handler falls back to existing slowpath when not enabled. No schema migrations.

Testing done: unit tests for controller logic, integration test that simulates KV eviction + heavy requests and asserts transition to fast-fallback, e2e canary in 'us-west-2' with 5 tenants gradually ramped to 200 req/s.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc linked (Linear ENG-2114)
- [x] Unit and integration tests added
- [x] Canary run completed and metrics collected
- [x] Telemetry dashboards updated

Rollout plan: feature flag rollout in two stages: (1) internal canary for 72h with increased telemetry retention, (2) staged rollout to 5% of production traffic for 24h, (3) ramp to 100% if no persistent fast-fallbacks observed. If persistent fast-fallbacks occur we will auto-revert the feature flag and open an incident.

Motivating incident reference: SUP-8421 (tenant KV drain induced circuit longevity), related follow-ups ENG-2199.
